# How do players with 100+ hours review PUBG between August and October 2026 differently from newcomers?

Between August and October 2026, players with 100 hours or more reviewed PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS more negatively than newcomers, with a negative review share of 37.2% compared to 30.3% for players with under 10 hours and 29.4% for those with 10 to under 100 hours [R220][R221][R222]. While both groups complained about cheating and performance [R233][R258][R259], players with 100+ hours focused on slow developer updates [R236], non-transparent publisher decisions [R242], and a September tournament controversy [R268][R330]. Newcomers focused on campers and aggressive monetization [R247][R259] while praising realistic gunplay and initial drop tension [R248][R257]. During a September 2026 review spike where negative share jumped to 78.0% [R115], veteran players heavily protested unfair tournament bans of professional players Himass and Tanvuu [R268][R330][R368], whereas newcomers participated less and expressed more general complaints [R366][R367].

## Timeline

*   **2026-07**: PUBG had 327150 average concurrent players, 792142 peak, and a 3.16 gain percentage [R120].
*   **2026-08-11**: The developer released Update 42.3, patch notes, and a map service report [R133].
*   **2026-08-12**: PUBG: Playgrounds launched with the August Update to help players discover and enjoy community-created modes through matchmaking [R136].
*   **2026-08-17**: The first set of 2026 PUBG Esports Global Partner Team Edition skins was introduced in collaboration with Gen.G, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, 17Gaming, eArena, and Virtus.pro [R142].
*   **2026-08**: Average concurrent players was 321321, peak was 771621, and the gain percentage was -1.78 [R121].
*   **2026-09-08**: The developer announced the PUBG x Jujutsu Kaisen collaboration [R155].
*   **2026-09-09**: Update 43.1, patch notes, and map service report were released [R158].
*   **2026-09-15**: The second drop of Team Edition skins was released in collaboration with Four Angry Men, Natus Vincere, Twisted Minds, Falcons, Anyone's Legend, and DN SOOPers [R170].
*   **2026-09**: Average concurrent players dropped to 306927, peak was 788224, and the gain percentage was -4.48 [R122]. Negative reviews spiked to 78.0% [R115], with a monthly sample including 41 negative reviews from players with <10h, 41 from 10-<100h, and 74 from >=100h [R366][R367][R368].
*   **2026-10-13**: Update 43.2, an October store update, a map service report, and the PUBG x Bentley collaboration were released [R197][R198][R200].
*   **2026-10**: Average concurrent players rose to 317800, peak was 806873, and the gain percentage was 3.54 [R123].

## What players are complaining about

Newcomers with low playtime complained about campers, poor performance, cheaters, aggressive monetization, and general dissatisfaction [R247][R251][R259]. In contrast, players with 100 hours or more complained about cheaters, no-recoil scripts in ranked play, poor performance, slow updates, and publisher decisions [R222][R233][R236].

The primary driver of negative reviews for players with 100 hours or more was the PUBG Asia Stars tournament incident, where professional players Himass and Tanvuu were banned [R268][R330][R368]. This sparked backlash particularly in English-language reviews, which reached 74.3% negative (223 negative out of 300 sampled) in September [R364] compared to 35.7% negative (107 negative out of 300 sampled) in Simplified Chinese reviews [R365]. English reviewers complained about anti-cheat failures, unfair rules, and alleged bias favoring Korean streamers over Vietnamese players [R293][R295][R305].

Here are three reviews illustrating these player perspectives:

*   **Newcomer (3.4 hours):** `"Boring camper game, gameplay focused on hiding shooting from behind and camping"` [R247]
*   **Veteran (910.7 hours):** `"too many cheaters :) no recoil scripts"` [R233]
*   **Veteran (21282.8 hours):** `"AFTER ME SPENDING 100k usd on this game and 20000 hours, pubg(korea) banned 2 best vietnamese players because of their own rules and mistakes in an exhibition match. They can not beat vietnamese teams so they banned the 2 best players. i hope pubg creators lose everything they have. This game is dea"` [R268]

## What the data can't answer

*   Official announcements do not explain why the negative review spike occurred in September 2026 [R155].
*   Player count data cannot confirm if the September 2026 controversy directly caused the decline in player average concurrent numbers [R122].
*   Steam reviews only represent players who write reviews.
*   SteamSpy owner estimates of 100000000 .. 200000000 are approximations [R243].
*   No console player data is included.
*   The developer motives are only known as stated in official announcements.

After two circuits in Seoul, the PUBG Global Series is moving to Shanghai, China. PGS Circuit 3, featuring PGS 7, PGS 8, and PGS 9, will take place across three weeks from August 5 to 23.

Circuit 3 also marks the beginning of the second half of the 2026 PGS season—and from this point forward, the numbers change. Every series in Circuits 3 and 4 will award twice as many PGS Points as the first half of the season. Hello players!

With the August Update, PUBG: Playgrounds is arriving as a new home where even more players can discover and enjoy community-created modes together.

 

 

Developer’s Comment

Until now, players have been able to create their own modes through the UGC Alpha feature in Custom Match. However, playing those creations with others required creators to gather people themselves and invite them to a Custom Match, making it difficult for their modes to reach a broader audience.

It was also difficult to browse modes created by other players, which made community-created content less accessible overall.

With this update, the feature is being expanded into PUBG: Playgrounds. Popular and entertaining player-created modes will be selected and featured on a dedicated page, where players can jump straight into them through matchmaking. Our goal is to make PUBG: Playgrounds easier to access and use, while giving creators even more motivation to build great modes.

The modes available through PUBG: Playgrounds will be updated monthly. We plan to source modes through a variety of channels and continue introducing new creations with each update.

R138.text:
PGS 7: Tournament Recap

With PGS 7 in the rear view mirror, we caught up with our PGS reporter Jisooboy to get their expert insights on why the tournament unfolded in the way it did!

​

"Life is C(Choice) between B(Birth) and D(Death)."

 

I brought a famous quote to kick things off. In PUBG, players land with bare hands, but the outcome is ultimately determined by the choices they make. On the perilous boundary between life and death, players have always carved out their own destiny through those crucial choices.

​

Numerous factors are considered when making these decisions, but the most critical of all is undoubtedly the Blue Zone. Whether you are a casual player or a pro, preferred drop zones or cities may shift depending on the flight path (plane trajectory). However, no one can predict where the Blue Zone will shrink once everyone hits the ground. Thus, navigating the Blue Zone has always been a realm of experience and intuition, never of absolute certainty.

 

Particularly, the classic Blue Zone settings we were all accustomed to underwent a massive overhaul with the Update 42.1 Patch on June 16, 2026. The durations of the early and final phases were shortened, the overall size of the safe zones was reduced, and the Blue Zone damage scale shifted from a distance-based system to a cumulative time-spent system. Most importantly, the land-prioritization algorithm that assisted safe zone generation was completely removed.

 

Due to this monumental shift, teams that traditionally relied on "circle-reading" and strategic macro-play as their primary strengths have struggled significantly. Strategic powerhouses like DN SOOPERS, Team Vitality, and Team Falcons were pushed to the brink, finding themselves relegated from the Group Stage to the Survival Stage. Although they eventually clawed their way into the Final Stage, none of them walked away with results they could truly be satisfied with.

 

This crisis was not unique to macro-heavy teams either. Even squads renowned for their raw skirmishing power and gunplay, such as T1 and Natus Vincere, failed to even qualify for the Final Stage. While we witnessed numerous moments where players were picked off while rotating under time pressure, the shrink in the initial Blue Zone's area also created clear pressure points where teams were forced to make high-stakes decisions much faster than before.

 

Specifically, as the Phase 4 Blue Zone—which heavily dictates the momentum of any match—introduced a higher degree of randomness, the historical circle-prediction data used by many teams has been completely rewritten. Let's look at a concrete example.

 

The Blue Zone behavior we previously knew is illustrated in \[Attachment 1]. Especially when the circle pulled over water or rivers, it was essential for teams to analyze the ratio of land—which had a higher probability of pulling the next circle away from the water—to predict Phase 4 and preemptively seize high-tier compounds or defensive ridges. In that meta, certain spots were classified as highly reliable, go-to strongholds for mid-to-late game macro, earning them the nickname "Science" because teams could blind-drop or rotate into them without a second thought.

 

However, with this Blue Zone reform patch, it is safe to say those "scientific rules" have vanished. Formulaic circle patterns have disappeared, and highly volatile, unpredictable circles have emerged. Consequently, the strategic value of early-centering or rushing to secure a central compound has been somewhat diluted. As shown in \[Attachment 2], despite the heavy presence of water, a massive portion of the sea remains engulfed inside the active safe zone.

 

Match Survival Statistics (At the 10-Minute Mark)

Furthermore, as the early-phase Blue Zone times were cut short and their areas reduced, players' rotation paths frequently overlapped. This has had a direct impact on the match survival rate. Below is the compiled data:

- 
GS: Group Stage / WS: Winners Stage / SS: Survival Stage / FS: Final Stage / GF: Grand Final
[/*]

 

To conduct this data analysis, I reviewed every single match across all previous PGS iterations, manually counting and recording the number of active players surviving at the exact 10-minute mark.

 

While the current sample size under the new Blue Zone settings is still somewhat limited, the rule change has clearly driven a statistically significant drop in early-game survival numbers. Overall, the survival rate has decreased. Notably, we observed a massive drop-off in survivor counts during the Final Stage and on the map Rondo. Given the high-stakes nature of the Final Stage compared to the Group, Winners, or Survival Stages, combined with Rondo's incredibly vast terrain, we saw several teams in PGS 7 opt for highly aggressive, early rotations or make high-risk, high-reward gambles.

 

This survival drop was not uniform across all stages and maps. By stage, the Group Stage actually saw a slight increase in survival, while the Winners and Survival Stages showed a minor drop of about 2 players. However, in the Final Stage, the survival rate plummeted by 5.4 players. This data suggests that the new Blue Zone doesn't simply force early engagements across the board; rather, its impact is amplified dramatically on specific maps and during higher-stakes stages.

 

Of course, a holistic analysis must account for several other variables. We must examine qualitative factors that cannot be captured by raw data alone—such as the specific map pool, participating team rosters, team-specific tactical playstyles and tendencies, hot-drop/landmark conflicts, starting flight paths, Phase 1 circle shapes, and stage-specific lobby dynamics. While PGS 7 is the only tournament played under the updated Blue Zone rules so far, we will undoubtedly secure more reliable data and stronger statistical significance once PGS 8 and PGS 9 are concluded.

 

PUBG Esports athletes are constantly fighting for survival, chasing the clock under extreme pressure. At times, they are forced into unavoidable compromises, and they often fall victim to incredibly unforgiving circle shifts. Nonetheless, the beauty of PUBG Esports is that these players will adapt, and today's defeated squad can easily become tomorrow's champion. Survival or elimination—on that knife-edge boundary, which team do you think will make the ultimate winning choice?

 

- Jisooboy

R151.text:
PGS 9: How Did Gen.G Become a Top Team?

In the wake of Gen.G’s dramatic PGS 9 tournament win, we enlisted the help of PUBG expert reporter Jisooboy to analyse what precisely led to their tournament win! Here’s what they had to say:

When people think of the greatest organizations in PUBG Esports, a few teams naturally come to mind. Among them is Gen.G Esports, the 2019 PGC champion and a storied organization that has represented PUBG Esports for years. Yet after winning PGC 2019, Gen.G struggled to produce meaningful results. Following a third-place finish at PGI.S 2021, the team failed to win a single title across the PCS ASIA series or any subsequent PGC. Despite multiple rebuilds year after year, its only notable result was a runner-up finish at EWC 2025. Gen.G clearly needed a change.

Perhaps that is why Gen.G entered this year with a different level of ambition. The team signed seoul Cho Gi-yeol and Salute Woo Je-hyeon, both members of the PGC 2023 championship roster, as well as diyy Daniel Noh Noh Eun-woo, who had delivered standout performances for Al Qadsiah. In particular, seoul and Salute had been regarded as one of Korea’s strongest duos, sending expectations among PUBG Esports fans sky-high.

But the result of that major rebuild was disastrous. Gen.G finished only fourth in the domestic PWS, while its chances of qualifying for PGC began to fade. The team missed the Finals four times—at PGS 1, 2, 5, and 7 in 2026—and across 123 PGS matches recorded just seven Chicken Dinners, 3.49 kills per match, and 789 average damage per match. The numbers did not lie. It would not have been an exaggeration to call Gen.G one of the weakest Partner Teams competing in PGS.

Sure enough, Gen.G opened the first PGS Circuit, Circuit 1, by missing the Finals three times in a row. Gen.G was not alone—many teams that had undergone major rebuilds were also struggling to find their footing—but three consecutive Finals misses in Circuit 1 was still a shocking result.

As a Global Partner Team, Gen.G had the advantage of guaranteed participation in the PGS Circuit and more opportunities to accumulate PGS Points. Even so, it was pushed aside by established Partner Teams and strong regional qualifiers, failing not only to break into the PGS top eight but even falling into the bottom tier of the standings. Considering Gen.G’s history on the international stage, it was a deeply disappointing run.

The crisis continued in PGS Circuit 2. Gen.G appeared to be turning things around with a sixth-place finish at PGS 4, only to finish 23rd at PGS 5 and miss the Finals once again. The swings could hardly have been more extreme. The team returned to the Finals at PGS 6, but finished just 13th overall. Without a dramatic turnaround in Circuit 3, direct qualification to PGC was becoming almost impossible to imagine.

In my view, there were two main reasons for Gen.G’s struggles. First, the team had not had enough time to build chemistry. Second, communication was not yet smooth. Individual skill was never the issue. Every player already had extensive international experience and an impressive career behind them.

Meanwhile, the 2026 PUBG Esports season began with PGS. Many teams had rebuilt their rosters in January 2026, and because the opening competition was an international event rather than a domestic league, the level of opposition was extremely high. In roughly two months, teams had to establish their approach to macro play, understand each new teammate’s tendencies, sharpen the precision of information sharing, and raise the level of their teamplay in fights.

For newly signed diyy in particular, the language barrier made it difficult to exchange information and coordinate opinions smoothly with his teammates. It was something that had surfaced across tournaments, scrims, personal streams, and Ranked play, and it did not look like an issue that could be solved overnight. Beyond the differences in how overseas and Korean players make comms, it is difficult to completely learn every in-game callout, terrain reference, and piece of slang in just a few months. A building called ‘Palgakjeong’ in Korea, for example, may be called ‘Wizard Tower’ overseas. Depending on the map, there can be hundreds of callouts like these.

As these issues accumulated, comms mistakes became more frequent and information took longer to relay, inevitably leading to repeated teamkills and in-game errors. While Gen.G worked through that process, rival teams steadily built their own careers and collected prize money. Gen.G could do little but watch from the sidelines.

After enduring all of those difficulties, signs of change finally began to appear for Gen.G in PGS Circuit 3. The team finished only 11th overall at PGS 8, but many of the issues that had been repeatedly pointed out were beginning to improve. The result itself was not strong, yet the quality of Gen.G’s play had changed significantly. Cleaner comms, pre-planned setups, and more precise approaches began to take shape. As the team reorganized its positions and role order, both survival time and the rate at which it secured Placement Points began to rise.

 

PGS 8 Finals DAY 1 MATCH 1 — Erangel

Looking at Gen.G’s Chicken Dinner in Finals DAY 1 MATCH 1 on Erangel, the team focused on keeping all four players alive by denying routes other teams could use and gathering information before winning the decisive fight. The closing sequence still showed some instability. Gen.G held the stronger position, but when information about each player’s situation was not shared quickly enough, dangerous moments like this could still occur. Even so, the match helped Gen.G sharpen its form as the tournament progressed.

 

PGS 8 Finals DAY 2 MATCH 2 — Erangel

The second highlight was how well the revised roles worked in tournament play. Gen.G’s typical losing pattern had often looked like this: ① Salute looks for an angle to hunt another team → ② if the opponent responds well or Gen.G cannot execute quickly as a team, Salute is neutralized → ③ BeaN and diyy try to help, only to get knocked in succession or draw a third party → ④ Seoul makes a big play at the end, but the team still goes down soon after.

 

Gen.G’s Typical Losing Pattern

Over time, however, the revised positioning and order changed that pattern. When Gen.G needed to look for a third-party angle or take the initiative and eliminate an opponent first, Seoul moved to the front, combining detailed reads of the situation with smooth, persistent pressure. BeaN and diyy acted as the glue in the middle, while Salute surveyed the wider battlefield from the backline and took responsibility for the final calls. The new structure began to pay off.

The role changes improved Gen.G’s overall survival time and Placement Point output. At the PGS 6 Grand Finals, Gen.G averaged only 1.4 Placement Points per match; by the PGS 9 Finals, that figure had risen to 3.9. The team’s average survival time also increased from 20 minutes 53 seconds to 22 minutes 38 seconds. Salute’s combat numbers, which had dipped somewhat after taking on the main IGL role, also began to recover. Team average damage jumped sharply from 672 to 980.

In a way, perhaps every problem Gen.G had faced ultimately came down to time. Salute, for example, moved from an attacking role into responsibility for the team’s calls, giving him far more to process and manage and preventing him from playing at his best. BeaN, serving as the glue of the team, needed above all to become a stable, mistake-free presence with the ability to survive tenaciously—and it took time to fully develop that role. Seoul was always elite statistically, but those numbers had largely been individual. There were moments when he needed to step forward before the team began to collapse. diyy, meanwhile, needed to reshape the entire style of play he had been accustomed to.

Gen.G’s strengths are now clear. The team had always built good scenarios for attacking opponents, but it lacked the finishing power and clearly defined roles needed to complete them. Now Seoul and Salute, two of the best players in the world, have fully settled into their respective roles, while BeaN’s survival instincts—honed over years in the PUBG scene—have matured into a major strength. Even diyy, who had repeatedly made costly mistakes, played the biggest role in delivering Gen.G the championship in the final match of the PGS 9 FINAL.

Salute’s Read of the Situation + Seoul’s Composed Finish

BeaN’s Brilliant Placement Defense

diyy’s Winning Play for the Championship

Of course, while this column was being written, it was announced that diyy had ended his contract and transferred to Team Liquid on August 25, 2026. Gen.G then announced another rebuild by signing taemin Kang Tae-min on August 27, 2026, one of the key players from the PGC 2019 championship roster. There is a chance that the gaps discussed above could emerge once again, but every player on Gen.G has the experience and skill to fill them, so there may be little reason for serious concern.

Closing

994 days.

That is how long Korean PUBG Esports had gone quiet on the international stage since its PGC 2023 championship. Gen.G, too, had to endure repeated failures and rebuilds while searching for a way back to the top. The players changed roles, learned to understand one another’s play, and endured countless rounds of trial and error before finally becoming one complete team. In the end, what made Gen.G a top team again was not a single signing or one special strategy. It was the time required to understand one another, the experience gained by enduring failure, and the determination of players who refused to give up until the very end.

After quietly enduring failure after failure, Gen.G finally lifted an international trophy. In doing so, one of PUBG Esports’ most storied organizations proved itself once again: a great team is not simply made—it is completed only after surviving countless failures. We remember all the losses they endured in order to become stronger. And those memories will only make Gen.G stronger still.

- Jisooboy

The PUBG Americas Series 2 Playoffs and Finals are nearly here! Across four weekends, 29 teams will compete twice for the chance to be crowned champions of the Americas. Bringing you all the action on a rotating basis is our brilliant, bombastic and iconic broadcast talent: Gibson, Porosaurus and Toffees.

The 29 teams are not the only ones with something to play for. By watching an official PUBG Americas Series 2 or PAS2 stream on Twitch or Kick, you can earn up to 12 unique PUBG item drops. A different item will be available each day, so make sure you tune in regularly if you want to complete the collection.

Check out our main PAS article for full details about Drops, Participating Teams, Schedule and more!

R164.text:
PUBG EMEA Championship: Meet The Teams of Playoffs 1!

The PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall Playoffs are about to kick off tonight at 18:00 CEST! 

Over the course of three match days this weekend, we will whittle down 29 teams into 16 finalists! Who will make the cut? 

The PEC: Fall Playoffs have a unique qualification format. On Day 1, the top 8 teams in the 16-team lobby will qualify straight to the Finals. Teams who miss out will have a second chance on Day 2 with an easier lobby - but there will only be 5 qualification spots up for grabs. Finally, on Day 3, the remaining 16 teams will face off for just 3 qualification spots. Every match counts - who will make the cutoff? Tune in on Twitch, Kick and YouTube from tonight at 18:00 CEST to find out.

An important update: the Twitch & Kick drops originally scheduled for this weekend have been postponed due to a technical issue and will instead be available during the Finals 2 Weekend, alongside the original planned Finals drops. This does not affect our G-Coin giveaway, which will continue during this weekend's broadcasts as usual. Find more information on our full blog here: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/578080/view/712285688032135377?l=english"][/dynamiclink]

Drop In: PUBG College Royale Returns for the Fall 2026 Season!

College PUBG competitors, get your squads ready—PlayVS and KRAFTON are teaming up once again to bring back PUBG College Royale for the Fall 2026 season!

This free-to-compete event is open to all college students in the U.S. and Canada. Sign up today before the first Qualifier on October 25. 

Below is everything you need to know about the upcoming season and how to get involved.

What’s at Stake?

We’re leveling up the rewards this season! Top-placing teams will compete for a share of $15,000 in scholarship awards, and on top of that, participants will have the opportunity to earn G-COIN, in-game items, and more just for competing!

Tournament Format

The tournament structure is designed to give teams multiple opportunities to stack up points and secure a spot in the championship:

- 
Three Open Qualifiers: Teams will compete across three separate open qualifier events. Each Open Qualifier consists of a 5-match series.
[/*]

Cumulative Leaderboard: Teams earn points based on their placement and performance in each Open Qualifier. Results are tracked on a leaderboard where points accumulate across all three opens.

The Top 16 Reach the Finals: The top 16 teams on the leaderboard will advance to the PUBG College Royale Finals. There, they will battle it out across 5 final matches live on stream to be crowned the Fall 2026 Champions and claim their share of the $15k prize pool!

R173.text:
PEC: Fall Finals 1: Drops, Participating Teams and more!

After an exciting weekend of qualifications (and non-qualifications) at last week’s Playoffs 1, it’s now almost time to crown our first (of two) PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall Champions!

Will reigning champions Virtus.pro and NAVI retain their tournament title, or will a new challenger usurp them? I guess you’ll just have to find out this weekend…

Here’s your look at the lobby:

S8UL

09

Team Vitality

S2G Esports

ACEND Club

PGG

Joga Bonito

noslack

Virtus.pro

Everlong

Bushido Wildcats

Big John

Twisted Minds

Vis

Natus Vincere

Team Kazakhstan

The PEC Finals are all about consistency. We play the classic SUPER format: three match days, and whoever has the most amount of combined kill points and placement points at the end of 15 matches will become the first PEC: Fall Champion!

PGC Points

Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PEC: Fall is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! With 32 teams competing and over $1,500,000 of prize pool on the line (not to mention bragging rights of being the best PUBG team in the world), it’s already shaping up to be a dramatic event. Make sure to tune in to the PEC: Finals to find out who will secure their tickets to the event!

PGC Host Wildcard

With PGC taking place in Türkiye, one team for the Türkiye region will also be selected to represent their nation as the host team - seeded directly into the Grand Finals in Istanbul from December 11 - 13. The team will be selected based on performances throughout the year and other criteria - so a strong performance in regional tournaments like PEC could be critical. 

Additionally, if a Turkish team qualifies for PGC via PGC Points, they will automatically receive the wildcard slot. The PGC Points slot will then be assigned to the next best ranked EMEA team in the PGC Points standings. If more than one Turkish team qualify for PGC via PGC Points directly, the top-ranked team will receive the Host Team Wildcard.

Drops

Even if a PEC: Fall tournament title or ticket to Istanbul isn’t in your future, you can still tune in and earn Drops by watching the broadcast live on Twitch and Kick! Each day this weekend there’s a new Drop up for grabs - reach 120 minutes of cumulative watch time on a PEC (or PAS, or both!) broadcast on any given day to unlock that day’s drop.

In addition, there will be G-Coin giveaways throughout the broadcast. Check the hints shared on our social media channels during the broadcast to uncover the codes!
 

PAS & PEC Finals 1

 Sep 18, 2026

How to unlock: watch a PEC or PAS stream for 120 minutes

PEC: from 18:00 CEST

PAS: from 4pm PDT / 7pm EDT

THE ORIGINAL IS BACK T-Shirt

 Sep 19, 2026

Peculiar Greeting

 Sep 20, 2026

PUBG Varsity Jacket

And in case you missed it: we had originally planned to also run drops during last weekend’s Playoffs broadcasts, but due to technical issues they were instead moved to the second Finals weekend (Oct 2 - 4). They’ll be available alongside the drops we originally planned, so be extra sure to tune in then for a weekend of double Drops. Mark your calendar!

PGC Host Wildcard

With PGC taking place in Türkiye, one team for the Türkiye region will also be selected to represent their nation as the host team - seeded directly into the Grand Finals in Istanbul from December 11 - 13. Virtus.pro and Team Falcons crowned PEC & PAS Finals 2 Champions!

Following an exciting 3 days of action last weekend at the PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall and PUBG Americas Series 2, Virtus.pro and Team Falcons were crowned as the Finals 2 Champions! 

Both teams finished the weekend with commanding leads over the rest of the pack. The weekend particularly represented a good return to form for Virtus.pro, who convincingly made up for their 13th place position in Finals 1 with a truly dominant performance in Finals 2 to sweep the lobby. In PAS, Team Falcons’ back-to-back 1st place in Finals 1 and Finals 2 is proof that the superstar squad has fully adapted to the 2026 competitive environment, and we’re excited to see if they can continue their momentum into PGS and PGC on the global stage later this year.

As always, regional PUBG Esports play has a large bearing on which teams can qualify to PGC, through those all-important PGC Points. A number of teams have already qualified directly to PGC through strong regional performances at PEC and PAS.

Qualified to PGC (through PGC Points earned at regional play):

EMEA

Americas

Virtus.pro

Team Falcons

Natus Vincere

Team Liquid

09

Godlike

Twisted Minds

Circle Nine

Of course, many of the teams listed above also have a strong possibility of also qualifying to PGC through a good performance at the upcoming PUBG Global Series Circuit 4. If, for example, Viruts.pro puts on a strong performance at the next PGS (and qualifies as a result), their original PGC qualification slot that they earned at PEC will then be redistributed to the next best team from their region’s PGC Points leaderboard. With Virtus.pro and Team Falcons already high in the PGS points table, this means we have a strong chance of seeing Acend Club and Copenhagen Wolves (and others) possibly qualify to PGC 2026.

As PGC 2026 takes place in Türkiye, there will also be a host region seed for a Turkish team. Stay tuned for more details!

If you want to find out who ultimately qualifies to PGC 2026, be sure to tune in to the upcoming PUBG Global Series tournaments!

PUBG Global Series 11: October 22 - 25

PUBG Global Series 12: October 29 - November 1

The Final Road to PGC begins: PGS Circuit 4!

Hello, PUBG Esports fans!

The final stretch of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is approaching: PGS Circuit 4. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the three remaining tournaments will bring this year’s 12-event PUBG Global Series to a close.

Circuit 4 is more than just the final circuit of the season. With the conclusion of PGS 12, the final PGS Points standings for the 2026 season will be determined, deciding the eight teams that will advance to PUBG Global Championship 2026.

After three circuits of competition, the race for PGC is beginning to take shape—but nothing has been decided yet. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and double points on the line at PGS 12, there are still 240 PGS Points up for grabs.

Which teams will earn their way to PGC 2026 through PGS Points? Let’s take a closer look at Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.

PGS Circuit 4 Schedule

PGS Circuit 4 will take place from October 14 to November 1.

- 
PGS 10

- 
Group Stage: October 14
[/*]
- 
Winners Stage: October 15
[/*]
- 
Survival Stage: October 16
[/*]
- 
Final Stage: October 17–18
[/*]
[/*]
- 
PGS 11

- 
Winners Stage: October 22
[/*]
- 
Survival Stage: October 23
[/*]
- 
Final Stage: October 24–25
[/*]
[/*]
- 
PGS 12

- 
Survival Stage: October 29
[/*]
- 
Grand Finals: October 30–November 1
[/*]
[/*]

As the Circuit Final, PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.

When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the 2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.

 

PGS Points Standings

With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.

At the conclusion of Circuit 3, Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points, followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.

Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.

But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.

Most importantly, Circuit 4 is still to come. The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.

 

PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points

The top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings, accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.

And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.

The team finishing 1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals. The 2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1, while the teams finishing 3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage.

This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.

 

240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs

In both PGS 10 and PGS 11, the winner will earn 60 PGS Points, with points awarded down through 16th place.

At the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the points will be doubled. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.

That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:

60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.

Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.

For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.

PGS 10 Groups

And it all begins with PGS 10.

The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.

PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.

- 
Group A: Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere
[/*]
- 
Group B: T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming
[/*]
- 
Group C: Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike
[/*]

\[Updated: October 12] 

Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.

※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.

The Final Step to PGC

The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.

There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.

Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the PGC Grand Finals?

The final competition of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is about to begin.

Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026!

PGS 10: The Predator, Virtus.pro

Until last year, it felt like the era of Twisted Minds. But this year, everything has changed. The arrival of a predator capable of devouring every team in its path has reshaped the PUBG Esports landscape. And that predator emerged not from Asia or APAC, but from Europe. Its name is Virtus.Pro (VP), the new dominant force in PUBG Esports.

​Of course, VP was not yet the finished product in 2025. The team finished as runners-up at PGS 9 and went on to claim the PGS 10 title. However, when it mattered most at PGC 2025, VP once again had to settle for second place. But the VP of 2026 is a different beast. Starting with a championship victory at PGS 3, VP followed up with a runner-up finish at PEC Spring, third place at PGS 5, and a championship title at the Esports World Cup (EWC). The team then secured back-to-back runner-up finishes at PGS 7 and PGS 8, followed by another second-place finish at PEC Fall. And last week, VP claimed yet another championship at PGS 10. VP now holds a commanding lead in the PGS Points standings and has consistently placed among the top teams at major tournaments throughout the year. So, what exactly has made VP so strong?

VP’s biggest transformation began in mid-2025. After announcing his retirement as a professional player, ibiza transitioned into a coaching role with VP, while curexi joined the roster to fill the vacant position. Having made his professional debut in 2018, ibiza competed until 2025 and established himself as one of Europe’s most experienced veterans. He had served as VP’s in-game leader (IGL), but decided to take on a new challenge as a coach to help the team reach the next level.

​To fill the gap, VP brought in curexi, who had previously played for prominent organizations such as Heroic and FaZe Clan, strengthening the team’s overall balance. As a coach, ibiza began applying the experience and strategic knowledge he had accumulated over his long career, providing tailored preparation for each tournament. Meanwhile, curexi quickly adapted to the existing roster, requiring little time to find his place within the team.

​So, what makes this team so formidable? VP has many strengths, but three stand out in particular.

The first is VP’s ability to make quick, accurate decisions under pressure. Lukarux, the team’s IGL, excels at identifying which positions to secure and which routes to take. Even when circumstances change in an instant, he remains composed and makes decisive calls. Whether attacking or defending, his decisions consistently demonstrate remarkable precision and stability. But these decisions do not come from Lukarux alone. In today’s competitive environment, every player must be capable of making independent decisions. At the same time, those individual decisions must align with the team’s overall strategy. Lukarux establishes the bigger picture, while the other three players make real-time adjustments and contribute the finer details needed to execute that strategy.

​As we will explore further, VP’s confidence in its fighting ability—and its understanding of which engagements it can win—forms the foundation of its decision-making. This is why VP often takes a far more aggressive approach than other teams. Once VP identifies a target, the team commits its full attention to it. Teams that fall behind in championship races sometimes struggle because they consider too many options at once, losing sight of what matters most at critical moments. VP is different. The team knows exactly what to prioritize when it matters, and more importantly, how to execute the actions required to achieve its objective.

​The second strength is VP’s exceptional fighting ability and technical skill. And to explain this, we have to talk about NIXZYEE. If I had to choose just one player with the most formidable fighting ability in 2026, I would pick NIXZYEE without hesitation. He possesses an extraordinary range of combat techniques and movement skills, combining devastating firepower with excellent teamwork.

​His precision when spraying with magnified scopes is almost mechanical. His peeks are astonishingly fast, and his unpredictable movement constantly disrupts his opponents’ timing. With his overwhelming individual skill, NIXZYEE turns every engagement into a nightmare for his opponents. Among all active players, it would not be an exaggeration to call him one of the most complete players in the game. What makes him even more frightening is his constant pursuit of improvement. He continues to study new techniques, refine them, and incorporate them into his gameplay.

​But NIXZYEE is far from VP’s only threat. Beami and curexi also bring tremendous firepower to long-range engagements, consistently delivering strong performances. They are particularly dangerous when using sniper rifles (SRs), often securing the first knock against an opponent and creating new opportunities for their team to push forward. Their headshot accuracy is especially impressive. While many professional players maintain headshot rates of around 20%, VP’s players frequently exceed 30%. These precise headshots allow them to knock opponents out of position and create opportunities to take control of areas held by enemy teams. These strengths were on full display at PGS 10. Throughout the tournament, VP recorded 55 first knocks, averaging 5.5 per match.

VP’s third major strength is its ability to build and execute strategies specifically designed to win championships. Its tactical flexibility goes beyond making adjustments within individual matches. VP also analyzes the overall standings, identifies its closest championship rivals, and develops strategies to directly challenge them when necessary. The final match of PGS 10 on Taego is a perfect example.

​At the time, VP was tied on 86 points with tournament leader Team Liquid (TL). Rather than simply following its usual strategy and trying to outscore its rival through conventional play, VP made a bold decision. It chose to directly target TL. This was not a reckless gamble. It was a calculated decision based on VP’s confidence in early-game engagements and its analysis of how TL was likely to respond. And the strategy worked almost immediately. VP eliminated two TL players in an early engagement, gaining a decisive advantage from the start. From there, VP systematically shut down the routes TL could use to move into the playable area, limiting its opportunities to recover and earn additional points. By neutralizing its closest rival, VP took control of the championship race. In the end, the title belonged to VP.

​Looking Ahead

There is still much more to explore when it comes to VP’s winning formula. But with even greater challenges waiting ahead, it would be a shame to reveal every aspect of their strategy just yet.

​The predator of 2026 has already conquered PGS. Can VP go one step further and finally lift the PGC trophy it has been chasing? We’ll be watching closely as the predator prepares for its next hunt.

​- Jisooboy

2027 PUBG Esports: What’s Changing

In 2027, PUBG Esports will introduce a new competitive structure.

With updates to the existing regional competition system and the introduction of four Phases throughout the year, we aim to create a new competitive environment where more teams can compete for a place on the global stage and prove their skills.

Take a closer look at the new competitive structure and key changes below.

Regional Competition Updates

In 2027, PUBG Esports will introduce changes to its regional competition structure, including the division of existing regions and the addition of a new region.

The existing EMEA region will be divided into Europe, Eurasia, and MENA, while the Americas will be divided into North America and South America. India, home to a massive community of PUBG fans and players, will join as a new competitive region, creating more opportunities for teams to compete on the global stage.

The race to qualify for PGS begins in each Regional League. Established teams and new challengers alike will compete at the regional level, with their results determining who advances to the global stage. With the updated regional competition structure, fans can look forward to new rivalries, new contenders, and more stories unfolding throughout the year.

Four Phases, Four Chances

PUBG Esports in 2027 will feature four Phases, from Phase 1 through Phase 4.

Each Phase consists of Regional Leagues and the corresponding PUBG Global Series (PGS).

- 
Phase 1: Regional League: Phase 1 → PGS: Phase 1
[/*]
- 
Phase 2: Regional League: Phase 2 → PGS: Phase 2
[/*]
- 
Phase 3: Regional League: Phase 3 → PGS: Phase 3
[/*]
- 
Phase 4: Regional League: Phase 4 → PGS: Phase 4
[/*]

 

Each Phase brings a fresh opportunity to qualify for PGS, and securing a spot in one Phase does not guarantee participation in the next. New challengers will have the chance to reach the global stage, while established teams must continue to prove themselves.

As part of this competitive restructuring, starting in 2027, the Global Partner Team (GPT) program will evolve into a partnership focused on collaborative in-game items and marketing activities. All teams, including existing GPT teams, will need to earn their place at PGS through their performance in each Phase’s Regional League, without guaranteed slots. Further details on the updated partnership will be shared in a future announcement.

The next chance is earned through performance. Each of the four Phases brings a fresh challenge, creating new stories on the global stage.

Introducing PUBG Esports Points

In 2027, PUBG Esports Points will replace the existing points systems. Previously, PGC Points were awarded based on Regional League results, while PGS Points were awarded based on PGS results. Under the new system, points will be awarded exclusively based on performance at PGS.

Teams will earn PUBG Esports Points based on their results at PGS. These points will accumulate throughout the year and count toward qualification for PGC. While the race from the Regional Leagues to PGS continues with each Phase, results achieved on the global stage will build throughout the year through PUBG Esports Points.

Further details on the points distribution and PGC qualification system will be announced separately.

2027 PUBG Esports Schedule

PUBG Esports in 2027 will begin with the Regional Leagues.

Phase 1 and Phase 2 will take place in the first half of the year, followed by the 2027 PUBG Nations Cup in July. Phase 3 and Phase 4 will continue in the second half of the year, before the year concludes with the 2027 PUBG Global Championship.

- 
Phase 1: Late March – Early May
[/*]
- 
Phase 2: Mid May – Mid June
[/*]
- 
2027 PNC: Early July
[/*]
- 
Phase 3: Early August – Mid September
[/*]
- 
Phase 4: Late September – Early November
[/*]
- 
2027 PGC: Late November – Early December
[/*]

* The schedule above is subject to change.

The changes coming in 2027 go beyond the competitive structure. Alongside the updated competition system, a new look for PUBG Esports is also on the way. Stay tuned for more updates as PUBG Esports prepares for 2027.

Further details on each Regional League’s schedule and format, PUBG Esports Points, and other tournament information will be shared in future updates.

Thank you.

PUBG Esports Team

After three circuits of competition, the race for PGC is beginning to take shape—but nothing has been decided yet. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and double points on the line at PGS 12, there are still 240 PGS Points up for grabs.

Which teams will earn their way to PGC 2026 through PGS Points? Let’s take a closer look at Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.

PGS Circuit 4 Schedule

PGS Circuit 4 will take place from October 14 to November 1.

As the Circuit Final, PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.

When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the 2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.

 

PGS Points Standings

With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.

At the conclusion of Circuit 3, Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points, followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.

Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.

But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.

Most importantly, Circuit 4 is still to come. The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.

 

PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points

The top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings, accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.

And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.

The team finishing 1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals. The 2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1, while the teams finishing 3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage.

This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.

 

240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs

In both PGS 10 and PGS 11, the winner will earn 60 PGS Points, with points awarded down through 16th place.

At the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the points will be doubled. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.

That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:

60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.

Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.

For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.

PGS 10 Groups

And it all begins with PGS 10.

The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.

PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.

The Final Step to PGC

The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.

There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.

Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the PGC Grand Finals?

The final competition of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is about to begin.

Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026!

R223.text:
我本来在PUBG里只想当个安静的人机质检员。原则很简单：不主动开枪，不抢队友空投，毒圈来了先找车，车炸了先找厕所。结果上周电竞社招新，社长非要看我账号，说“随便看看战绩”。我手一抖，把最近十场记录投到了教室大屏上——十场零杀，场均伤害18，最高排名第二，系统称号“苟活专家”。全班沉默两秒，后排有人喊：“姐，你这运营太稳了吧？”我还没解释那是我边吃泡面边玩的，社长已经拍桌子：“明天校际四排赛，你来当指挥。”我说我连枪都压不住，他说：“要的就是你这种不吃资源还能进决赛圈的。”更离谱的是第二天，学校论坛冒出一个热帖：《电竞社新指挥场均伤害18，疑似隐藏战术大师》。底下有人回“18伤害怎么了，人家用脑子打游戏”，还有人问“学姐收徒吗，我枪法好，听指挥”。从那天起，我课桌里开始出现能量饮料和止痛药，都是男生塞的，说“指挥要保重身体”。我去食堂打饭，选修课坐我后排的两个男生端着餐盘坐我对面，问我：“你平时跳P城还是G港，我跟你。”我说我一般跳野区厕所，他眼睛一亮：“果然是细节控。”晚上更夸张，我一上线，邀请列表跟食堂排队一样。我随便进了一个队，里面三个男生，一个说“我负责架枪”，一个说“我负责开车”，还有一个说“我负责给你报点”。我说：“你们这么强为什么还要我？”他们异口同声：“缺个会苟的。”那天决赛圈，我全程趴在草丛里，连开镜都不敢，结果他们三个把对面灭了，最后一只鸡稳稳落我头上。其中一个男生还发语音：“指挥，这波圈刷得怎么样？”我说：“挺好，就是草有点扎脸。”他们笑成一片。后来事情彻底跑偏。有人把我“0杀吃鸡”的记录印成了传单，贴在宿舍楼下，标题是《想学运营吗？本周四晚，跟18伤害学姐学进圈》。我路过的时候，旁边两个男生小声说：“就是她，听说她连平底锅都不捡，因为怕影响走位。”我想解释，其中一个已经掏出手机：“学姐，能加个好友吗？我保证不给你丢空投。”现在我最怕的不是决赛圈一打四，也不是队友倒地喊救命，而是每天打开游戏，面对一堆“你指挥就行，枪我们来开”的邀请。
那一刻我终于明白，PUBG里最难压的不是枪，是全校想跟我一起跳厕所的热情。
